passages.text: But perhaps someone will say, “What does being baptized in water contribute to reverence?” First, you do what God determined. Second, being born again out of water to God, out of fear you exchange the first birth that came to you through desire, and thus you can attain salvation; otherwise it is impossible. For the prophet swore to us in this way, saying, “Truly I tell you, unless you are born again in living water, into the name of Father, Son, Holy Spirit, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.” Therefore come. For there is something merciful there, borne upon the water from the beginning, .... those baptized with the thrice-blessed naming, and rescues them from the punishment to come, offering to God, as gifts, the good deeds of the baptized themselves from their baptism onward. Therefore take refuge in the water, for this alone can quench the onrush of fire. The person not yet willing to come to it still bears the spirit of madness, because of which he is unwilling to come to “living water” for his own salvation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αἰτίᾳ φόβου τὴν ἐξ ἐπιθυμίας πρώτην σοι γενομένην καταλλάσσεις γένεσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: out of fear you exchange the first birth that came to you through desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: Fear motivates the exchange; desire characterized the first birth. The replacement birth is the stated water-rebirth; physical birth is not explicitly labeled sinful.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐὰν μὴ ἀναγεννηθῆτε ὕδατι ζῶντι, εἰς ὄνομα πατρός, υἱοῦ, ἁγίου πνεύματος
lexical_decisions.chosen: unless you are born again in living water, into the name of Father, Son, Holy Spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Follows this quotation’s wording, not the wording of a familiar canonical verse; no unprinted conjunctions are inserted into the name sequence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: borne upon the water from the beginning, .... those baptized
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly four printed gap dots remain. The missing predicate governing those baptized is not restored, leaving the English visibly interrupted.
Naming or invocation associated with baptism, described as thrice-blessed; no later doctrinal explanation is added.
Preserves the historical author’s spirit-language; λύσσα is raging madness, also rabid frenzy, not a supplied modern clinical diagnosis.

source_issues.issue: Exactly four printed dots mark unavailable wording. The governing predicate before those baptized is left interrupted; no reconstruction is supplied.

passages.text: Come, then, whether you are righteous or unrighteous. For if you are righteous, all you lacked was to be baptized for salvation. But if unrighteous, in addition to being baptized for the forgiveness of things done in ignorance, doing good remains for you in addition to baptism, in proportion to your impiety. Therefore, whether you are righteous or unrighteous, hurry to be born to God, for delay brings danger because the time appointed for death is unknown. Through doing good, show your likeness to the Father who begets you out of water, honoring the true God as Father as one who loves truth. Honor to him is for you to live as he, being righteous, wills; the will of the righteous is not to act unjustly. Injustice is murdering, committing adultery, hating, coveting, and things like these; and there are many forms of these.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ ἀναλογίαν τῆς ἀσεβείας ἡ ἐπὶ τὸ βάπτισμα εὐποιΐα
lexical_decisions.chosen: doing good remains for you in addition to baptism, in proportion to your impiety
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains proportional doing-good in addition to baptism, neither rewriting baptism as merely symbolic nor deleting the required deeds.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ ἐξ ὕδατος γεννῶντί σε πατρί, διὰ τῆς εὐποιΐας τὴν ὁμοιότητα δείξας
lexical_decisions.chosen: Through doing good, show your likeness to the Father who begets you out of water
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves water-birth and likeness through conduct without supplying a further causal mechanism.

passages.text: Yet one must add to these something that does not concern dealings with human beings but belongs specifically to the worship of God. I mean keeping clean: not having intercourse with one’s own wife when she is menstruating, because God’s law commands this. What then? If keeping clean did not belong also to God’s worship, you would gladly roll about like beetles. Therefore, as human beings possessing something beyond the irrational animals—being rational—cleanse your heart of evils through heavenly reasoning, and wash your body with a bath. For keeping clean is truly good, not because bodily purity takes precedence over cleansing of the heart, but because cleanliness follows goodness. Our teacher even exposed some of the Pharisees and scribes among you as hypocrites, although they are set apart and, as scribes, know the laws better than others, because they purified only what is visible to people but neglected the pure things of the heart, visible to God alone.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ ἐν ἀφέδρῳ οὔσῃ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γαμετῇ μὴ κοινωνεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: not having intercourse with one’s own wife when she is menstruating
lexical_decisions.rationale: Makes the euphemistic monthly-separation term intelligible without embellishment; this is the ancient author’s restriction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς οἱ κάνθαροι ἡδέως ἂν ἐκυλίεσθε
lexical_decisions.chosen: you would gladly roll about like beetles
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the comparison without supplying the substance in which the beetles roll.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐχ ὡς ὅτι προηγεῖται τῆς κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν κάθάρσεως ἡ τοῦ σώματος ἁγνεία
lexical_decisions.chosen: not because bodily purity takes precedence over cleansing of the heart
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the denial of bodily priority and the simultaneous affirmation of bodily cleanliness.

passages.text: So he truly used this express statement toward their hypocrites, not toward all of them. For he even said that some should be listened to, because they had been entrusted with Moses’ seat. But to the hypocrites he said, “Woe to you, hypocritical scribes and Pharisees, because you clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside it is full of filth. Blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that their outsides too may become clean.” And this is true. For when the mind has been enlightened by knowledge, the person who has learned can be good, and becoming clean follows this. Good care for the outward body comes from the inward understanding. Just as inattention to the body cannot produce care for the mind, so the person who is clean inside can also clean the outside. But the one who cleans the outside does this with regard to people, looking toward praise, and with the praise of the onlookers has nothing before God.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπό γε τῆς κατὰ τὸ σῶμα ἀναισθησίας τῆς διανοίας πρόνοια γενέσθαι οὐ δύναται
lexical_decisions.chosen: inattention to the body cannot produce care for the mind
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀναισθησία can be lack of feeling, perception, or concern. Inattention is preferred in the care argument; bodily insensibility remains an alternative. The text is not changed to a word meaning washing or cleanliness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ἐπαίνῳ τῶν ἱστορούντων παρὰ τῷ θεῷ οὐδὲν ἔχει.
lexical_decisions.chosen: and with the praise of the onlookers has nothing before God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the contrast between human praise and standing before God without adding a specified reward.

passages.text: Who does not see that it is better not to come together with a woman during her monthly condition, but after she has become clean and been immersed? And after intercourse one must also immerse oneself. If you shrink from doing this, recall how you pursued the parts of purity when you worshiped insensible idols. Be ashamed that here, where you ought to undertake not, I say, something greater, but simply the whole of purity, you become more reluctant. So consider the one who made you act there, and you will understand who it is that puts reluctance toward purity into you here.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after she has become clean and been immersed
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this repeated purity setting βαπτίζω denotes bodily immersion; the same verb is baptized in the initiation setting. The contextual gloss difference does not claim different Greek words.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after intercourse one must also immerse oneself
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains repeated immersion after sexual intercourse, not mere inward purity or a newly asserted doctrine of repeated initiation.
